# Openia — Correctness Assessment of Code Generated by LLMs Using Internal Representations

- **Citation** — Tuan-Dung Bui, Thanh Trong Vu, Thu-Trang Nguyen, Son Nguyen,
  Hieu Dinh Vo (VNU University of Engineering and Technology, Hanoi).
  *Correctness Assessment of Code Generated by LLMs Using Internal Representations.*
  arXiv:2501.12934 (2025). Code: https://github.com/iSE-UET-VNU/OPENIA
- **Relation to Ribeiro et al. 2512.07404** — same *topic* (internal rep of code
  correctness), **different group and different method**. Openia is a *supervised
  probe on the model's own generations*; Ribeiro is *unsupervised contrast-pair
  RepE/LAT*. Read them as the two methodological poles for our probe family choice.

## TL;DR

White-box framework: read an LLM's hidden states **while it generates code** and
train a small supervised probe to predict whether that generation is correct,
before any test runs. Beats post-hoc black-box classifiers (CodeBERT, CodeT5+)
and LLM-as-judge. Middle layers + last generated token carry the signal.

## Method (the bits we'd borrow)

- **Supervised** probe (not contrast-pair). Lightweight MLP: 2 hidden layers
  (128, 64), binary correct/incorrect head. 50 epochs, bs=32, lr=1e-3.
- **Token aggregation:** last generated *code* token's hidden state works best;
  optionally **concatenate** across selected layers/tokens for more signal.
- **Layer:** middle layers (≈16–28) optimal; shallow=syntactic, last layer
  declines. Code Llama layer 16: F1≈0.74–0.78; layer 1: F1=0.59.
- **Setting that matters for us:** probes the model's **own generated code**
  (generation-time states), not code pasted into the prompt.

## Results (numbers worth comparing against)

Models: DeepSeek-Coder 1.3B/6.7B, Code Llama 7B/13B, Magicoder 7B. Benchmarks:
HumanEval (164), MBPP (500), **DevEval (1,825 repo-level)**; 24,890 labeled units.

- Independent-unit (cross-task): acc/F1 **0.73–0.79** vs CodeT5+ 0.66–0.70,
  CodeBERT 0.64–0.68. Up to **+23%** rel. over post-hoc methods.
- Repo-level (DevEval): F1 **0.73–0.83**; up to **3×** for DeepSeek-1.3B
  (0.83 vs 0.27). Up to **+40%** over LLM-Check.
- Cross-language avg F1 0.75 (TypeScript best 0.88, Python worst 0.67).
- **Data-efficient:** ~60% of training data → near-optimal F1 (0.77).
- Inference 0.6 ms/unit.

## Notes / relevance to us

- **Our supervised-probe lineage's nearest neighbor.** Their MLP-on-last-token
  is close to our `train_probe.py`; their layer/token findings are direct
  guidance for our layer-selection question.
- **Generation-time framing** = our complication (1): probes states from the
  model *writing* code. Contrast with Ribeiro (reading) and with our current
  input-stream framing. Useful when we test reading-vs-generation directions.
- **Repo-level via DevEval** addresses Ribeiro's single-function limitation —
  relevant if our downstream AI-control scenarios involve multi-component code.
- **Caveats they state:** cross-benchmark prompt sensitivity (−12% acc, 0.79→0.67);
  weak on runtime errors (static-only signal); ≤13B models only; no error
  localization (binary only); weakest on mid-difficulty tasks (F1 0.60).
